To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ANI package provides a new approach for a more accurate determination of the energy spectra and elemental composition of cosmic rays, based on the analysis of the EAS data, which is more reliable than the traditional methods.
1. The ANI package is a powerful and convenient tool to perform a multivariate analysis.

the elemental composition determination of primary cosmic rays based on the measurements of the EAS components at sea level and mountain altitudes is possible to an accuracy of 10–15% in the primary energy range from 10 14 eV to 10 17eV.

the following problems: (i) the development of new statistical methods for a more accurate analysis of EAS data; (ii) the comparison of the results of different EAS experiments; and (iii) the development of a new method to measure primary cosmic ray energy spectra and elemental composition.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the elemental composition determination is possible with a reasonable accuracy.
the elemental composition determination is possible at sea level with an accuracy of about 20%, and at mountain altitudes with an accuracy of 5-7%.
the elemental composition determination on sea level is possible with a reasonable accuracy, while the primary energy determination is not feasible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ANI multivariated statistical analysis and the modern EAS simulation program CORSIKA can be successfully used to determine the energy spectrum and elemental composition of the primary cosmic rays.
the new methods of data analysis and the use of new detectors will improve the accuracy of the primary energy spectra and elemental composition measurements.

a combination of modern EAS simulations with multivariate data analysis techniques can lead to significant improvements of the accuracy of the elemental composition determinations and the primary energy estimations.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the combination of modern EAS detectors with modern statistical methods allows us to achieve the accuracies in the determination of the elemental composition of primary cosmic rays and the primary energy estimations that are comparable with the accuracies obtained at the highest energies by the Pierre Auger Observatory.
the combination of the modern simulation and data analysis tools can be used for an efficient determination of the elemental composition of cosmic rays in the 10 14 to 10 17 energy range.

the combined use of the ANI package and the CORSIKA program provides the possibility to perform a detailed event-by-event analysis of the EAS data, and to improve considerably the accuracy of the primary energy spectrum and elemental composition determinations.
